record.title: incident retro for the phishing wave
record.summary: The team held an incident retrospective regarding last week's phishing wave. The incident response timeline showed 38 minutes between the first reported click (09:14) and the first containment action (09:52). Marcus noted a process gap where 11 minutes were lost waiting for him to exit a meeting, leading to a decision to create a documented escalation runbook that does not route through a single person. Regarding scope, 214 users received the email, 9 clicked, and 3 entered credentials on a fake ADFS page. All three users reset their credentials within the hour, and no successful logins from the attacker infrastructure were observed. Rio noted that the finance group still has an exemption from phishing-resistant MFA due to the ERP migration, but since the ERP vendor now supports FIDO keys, the exemption can be removed via a configuration change and communications plan. Rio will pilot this with five finance users next week before rolling it out to the rest of the group. Priya has already added the phishing domains to the blocklist feed and sent a takedown request to the registrar. For detection, Rio suggested implementing a canary token in the login footer template to catch clones immediately. Finally, Marcus noted that users who reported the incident received no acknowledgment; implementing auto-acknowledgment on the report button was suggested and added to the backlog.
